delete.description: MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Deletes a journal entry. Automatically-generated journals linked to a source record, and journals dated inside a closed financial period, cannot be deleted.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Journal id to delete.

message.description: Confirmation message including the deleted journal number.

400.description: Bad Request — the journal date falls within a closed financial period.

404.description: Not Found — missing journal, no delete permission, or an auto-generated journal that cannot be deleted.

message.description: Returned when the journal does not exist, the caller lacks delete permission, or the journal is an auto-generated entry that cannot be deleted.

500.description: Internal Server Error — the delete could not be completed.

put.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Updates an existing journal entry and replaces its line items.

**Amounts.** Send the line amounts as `currency_debit` / `currency_credit`, in the journal's currency. The base-currency `debit` / `credit` fields are derived by the server (`currency_* x currency_rate`) and anything sent in them is overwritten - a payload that carries only `debit` / `credit` has every line discarded and is rejected with `400`.

**Line items are a full replacement.** The `JournalTransaction` array is the complete set: a line with `id` updates that line, a line without `id` is inserted, and any existing line missing from the array is deleted. A line `id` that belongs to a different journal is rejected with `400`.

**Balance.** The sum of `currency_debit` must equal the sum of `currency_credit`; `total_debit` and `total_credit` on the journal are recomputed from the lines and cannot be set directly.

The `{id}` in the URL identifies the journal. `Journal.id` in the body is optional, but when present it must match the URL id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Journal REF # to update

id.description: Journal REF #. Optional - the `{id}` in the URL is authoritative. If you do send it, it must equal the URL id, otherwise the request is rejected with `400`.

date.description: Journal date. Must fall inside an open financial period, otherwise the request is rejected. Omit to keep the current date.

currency_code.description: Currency of the entry. **Always send it** - every line item's `currency_code` is overwritten with this value, so omitting it blanks the currency on all lines.

manual_currency_rate.description: Explicit FX rate from `currency_code` to the site's base currency. Omit (or send `null`) to let the server resolve the rate for `date`. Do **not** send `0` or `""`.

alter_description.description: Overridden description, used for auto-generated journals. Ignored when it equals `description`.

number.description: Journal number. Auto-generated; send it only to override.

attachment.description: Comma-separated file ids to keep attached. **Omitting it detaches the journal's existing attachments**, so send the current ids when you do not intend to change them.

total_debit.description: **Read only** - recomputed from the line items on every save. Anything sent here is ignored.

total_credit.description: **Read only** - recomputed from the line items on every save. Anything sent here is ignored.

currency_debit.description: **Read only** - total debit in the journal's currency, recomputed from the line items.

currency_credit.description: **Read only** - total credit in the journal's currency, recomputed from the line items.

staff_id.description: **Read only on edit** - the creating staff is preserved.

entity_type.description: **Read only** - set only for auto-generated journals.

entity_id.description: **Read only** - set only for auto-generated journals.

is_automatic.description: **Read only** - `1` when the journal was generated from another transaction.

created.description: Time of creation for the journal

modified.description: Last time this journal was updated

JournalTransaction.description: The **complete** set of line items for this journal. This array replaces the existing set: a line carrying `id` is updated, a line without `id` is inserted, and **any existing line whose id is absent from the array is deleted**. At least two lines are required, and the sum of `currency_debit` must equal the sum of `currency_credit` (tolerance 0.001) or the request is rejected with `400`.

id.description: Existing journal transaction REF #. Send it to **update** that line; omit it to **insert** a new line. The id must belong to this journal - a line id from another journal is rejected with `400`.

journal_account_id.description: Journal Account REF # to post this line to. Get it from [GET Journal Accounts](/15115326e0). A line with no `journal_account_id` is discarded.

currency_debit.description: Debit amount **in the journal's currency**. This is the field the API reads for the debit side - not `debit`. Send `0` for a credit line.

currency_credit.description: Credit amount **in the journal's currency**. This is the field the API reads for the credit side - not `credit`. Send `0` for a debit line.

alter_description.description: Overridden description, used for auto-generated journals. Ignored when it equals `description`.

tax_id.description: Tax applied to this line. Get it from [GET Taxes](/15115346e0). When set, the server splits the amount and generates an additional tax line for you.

debit.description: Debit amount in the site's base currency. **Read only - derived as `currency_debit * currency_rate`.** Anything sent here is overwritten.

credit.description: Credit amount in the site's base currency. **Read only - derived as `currency_credit * currency_rate`.** Anything sent here is overwritten.

currency_code.description: Currency Code. Read only in practice - every line is forced to `Journal.currency_code`.

currency_rate.description: FX rate used for this line. **Read only** - resolved by the server from `Journal.date`, or from `Journal.manual_currency_rate` when supplied.

subkey.description: Transaction sub-key. **Read only** - set by the server for auto-generated lines (taxes, client/supplier postings).

journal_id.description: Journal REF #. **Read only** - taken from the journal being edited.

created.description: Time of creation for this transaction

modified.description: Last time this transaction was updated

post.description: MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Creates a manual journal entry. Send the `Journal` header fields and the `JournalTransaction[]` double-entry lines. The total debit of the lines must equal the total credit, and at least one line is required. Amounts are supplied per line via `currency_debit` / `currency_credit` (in the journal currency); the base-currency `debit`/`credit` and the journal totals are calculated automatically. The journal `date` must fall within an open financial period.

post.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Create a journal category — a folder in the chart of accounts that groups other categories and posting accounts.

This endpoint creates **categories only**. To create a posting account that journal entries can be booked to, use *Add New Journal Account* instead; an `account_type` sent in this request is ignored.

**Required:** `code` and `name`.

`code` must be **numeric**, and it must not already be used by another category **or** by a journal account — codes are shared across both. Use *GET All Journal Cats* and *GET All Journal Accounts* to find a free code; by convention a child's code extends its parent's (a child of `5` is numbered `51`, `52`, …).

> **A code that is already in use does not return an error.** The request answers with `302` and a `Location` header pointing at the chart-of-accounts page, and no JSON body — so check that the code is free before posting, and configure your client not to follow redirects for this call.

Omit `journal_cat_id` to create a top-level category, or set it to the reference of the parent category to nest this one beneath it.

Only the `JournalCat` object is read from the request body; any other top-level object is ignored. `Content-Type` must be `application/json`; another content type, or a body that is not valid JSON, returns `500`.

> **Do not send `id` when creating.** If it holds the reference of an existing category, that category is overwritten instead of a new one being created. Use the *Edit Journal Cats* endpoint to change an existing category.

Requires the *Manage Journal Accounts* permission.

On success the endpoint responds with `202 Accepted` and the reference of the new category.

code.description: Code of the category. **Numeric only.** Must not already be used by another category or by a journal account. By convention a child's code extends its parent's — a child of category `5` is numbered `51`, `52`, and so on. A code that is already in use makes the request answer with `302` rather than a validation error.

name.description: Name of the category, as it appears in the chart of accounts.

type.description:
The normal balance side of the category — which side increases it. Defaults to `0` (Credit) when omitted, so set it explicitly: asset and expense categories are Debit, while liability, income and equity categories are Credit.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Credit |
| 1 | Debit |

journal_cat_id.description: Reference of the parent category. Omit, or send `-1`, to create a top-level category. Take the value from *GET All Journal Cats* — this is the parent's reference, not its `code`.

branch_id.description: Branch the category belongs to. Defaults to your current branch when omitted. Must reference an active branch, otherwise the category is rejected. Only relevant when branches are enabled for your account.

entity_type.description: Marks the category as one of the account tree's built-in categories. **Leave empty for a category you create yourself** — a category carrying this marker is treated as a system default and cannot be deleted. Values name the built-in groups of the chart of accounts (asset, liability, equity, income and expense groups, and the groups that hold treasuries, banks, stores, clients, suppliers, taxes and depreciation).

entity_id.description: Reference of the record identified by `entity_type`. Only meaningful when `entity_type` is also set.

disabled.description:
Whether the category is disabled.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Active (default) |
| 1 | Disabled |

id.description: Reference of the category. **Omit when creating.** If you send the reference of an existing category, that category is overwritten instead of a new one being created. Returned in the response as `id`.

parent_cat_ids.description: Comma-separated references of every ancestor category, ending with the immediate parent. Derived from `journal_cat_id`; any value sent is overwritten.

level.description: Depth of the category in the account tree. Recalculated automatically after the category is saved.

staff_id.description: Staff member associated with the category. Not populated when a category is created through the API.

total_debit.description: Accumulated debit total of the category. Maintained automatically from the journal entries posted beneath it; any value sent is ignored.

total_credit.description: Accumulated credit total of the category. Maintained automatically from the journal entries posted beneath it; any value sent is ignored.

is_recalculated.description: Whether the category's totals are up to date. Maintained automatically.

last_transaction_update.description: When the category's totals were last recalculated. Maintained automatically.

is_hidden.description:
Whether the category is hidden in the chart of accounts. Maintained automatically.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Visible |
| 1 | Hidden |

modified.description: When the category was last updated.

302.description: The `code` you sent is already used by another category or journal account. The response carries no body — only a `Location` header pointing at the chart-of-accounts page. Check the code is free before posting, and do not follow redirects for this call.

Location.description: The chart-of-accounts page the request was redirected to.

400.description: The category was rejected. Common causes are a missing or non-numeric `code`, a missing `name`, a suspended `branch_id`, or — on accounts that require every category to be assigned to a branch — a missing branch selection. `message` is `null` on this path; the detail is in `validation_errors`.

The request body is a flat JSON object. The account layer applies **no field validation** here, so the only hard requirements are the two fields the database cannot default: `cost_center_id` and `cost_center_ids`. Omitting either fails with a `400`.

In practice you should always send `name` and `code` as well — if omitted they are silently stored as an empty name and an empty/`0` code, which is rarely useful. `code` must be **unique** across the account; a duplicate `code` fails with a `400`.

`is_primary` marks a cost center as primary (root) or secondary (child):

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | Primary (root) |
| 0 | Secondary (child); defaults to `0` when omitted |

`cost_center_id` is the id of the parent cost center — send `0` for a primary/root cost center, or the parent's id for a child. `cost_center_ids` is the comma-separated ancestor path of parent ids; it **must be non-empty** (an empty string is rejected), and it is not maintained automatically, so the caller supplies it.

`branch_id`, `status`, `id`, `created` and `modified` are assigned by the server and are not settable through this endpoint.

On success the response is `{ "message": "...", "id": <new id> }`. The message is localized to the caller's language (for example `Cost center Added Successfully` in English).

| Parameter | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `page` | Page number (default `1`). |

| `filter[<field>][<operator>]` | Filter by a field, e.g. `filter[client_id][equal]=2`. |

post.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Creates a new booking (an appointment-style record). Provide the client, the booking date, and one or more services to book.

Each entry in `InvoiceItem` must reference an **active bookable service** — a product of type *Service* that has a duration configured and belongs to at least one category. A request whose services are not valid bookable services is rejected with `Please Enter Valid Service`.

The end time is calculated automatically from the services' durations, and the booking's staff and status are assigned automatically — you do not send them. Set `Invoice.convert` to `1` to immediately convert the new booking into an invoice within the same request; the response then also returns `invoice_id`.

The `.json` extension is optional and does not change the response.

client_id.description: Required. The id of an existing client the booking is for.

date.description: Required. The booking date in `dd/mm/yyyy` format.

start_time.description: Optional. Start time in 24-hour `HH:mm` format. Defaults to the start of the day when omitted.

description.description: Optional. Free-text note stored on the booking.

branch_id.description: Optional. The branch the booking belongs to. Defaults to the request's current branch.

convert.description: Optional. Set to `1` to also convert the created booking into an invoice in the same request; the response then includes `invoice_id`. Defaults to `0`.

InvoiceItem.description: The services to book. At least one is required and each must reference an active bookable service product.

product_id.description: Required. The id of a bookable service product (type *Service*, with a duration and a category).

200.description: The booking was created. Note this endpoint returns a `{code, message, id, appointment_id}` object (not the standard result envelope). When `Invoice.convert` was `1`, `invoice_id` is also returned; if the conversion failed, an `error` message is returned instead of `invoice_id`.

code.description: Result code (`200`).

id.description: The id of the created booking.

appointment_id.description: The id of the appointment created for the booking.

invoice_id.description: Only present when `Invoice.convert` was `1` and conversion succeeded — the id of the invoice created from the booking.

400.description: The booking could not be created. Two cases: an invalid bookable service returns `{ code: 400, errors: "Please Enter Valid Service" }`; a save failure returns `{ code: 400, message: ... }`.

code.description: Result code (`400`).

errors.description: Present when a booked service is not a valid bookable service.

message.description: Present when the booking itself could not be saved.

delete.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Deletes a booking by its id. A booking can only be deleted when you have permission and it has **not** already been converted to an invoice — otherwise the request is rejected. Deleting a booking also removes its linked appointment.

The `.json` extension is optional.

parameters.name: bookingId
parameters.description: The id of the booking to delete.

400.description: The booking could not be deleted — you lack permission, or it has already been converted to an invoice.

404.description: No booking exists with the given id.

get.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Changes the status of a booking. Pass the booking id and the target status code in the path.

| Value | Status |
|---|---|
| 0 | Pending |
| 1 | Confirmed |
| 2 | Invoiced (set automatically when the booking is converted to an invoice) |
| 3 | Cancelled |
| 4 | Done |

Typically you set `1` (Confirmed), `3` (Cancelled), or `4` (Done). The request always responds with HTTP 200 carrying an `error` flag: `error` is `false` when the status was changed, and `true` when it was not (for example an unsupported status, or a booking already converted to an invoice). A booking id that does not exist returns 404.

The `.json` extension is optional.

parameters.name: bookingId
parameters.description: The id of the booking whose status is being changed.

parameters.name: bookingStatus
parameters.description: Target status code. `0` Pending · `1` Confirmed · `2` Invoiced · `3` Cancelled · `4` Done.

200.description: Always returned (HTTP 200) whether or not the change applied — check the `error` flag. Success: `{"message":"Status Changed Successfully","error":false}`. Not applied: `{"message":"","error":true}`.

message.description: Result message. Empty when the change was not applied.

error.description: `false` when the status was changed; `true` when it was not applied (unsupported status, or booking already converted).

404.description: No booking exists with the given id.

MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Converts a booking into an invoice. On success it returns the id of the newly created invoice and marks the booking as *Invoiced*.

The conversion is rejected when the booking is cancelled, already converted, or missing required data. A booking id that does not exist returns 404.

The `.json` extension is optional.

400.description: The booking could not be converted — it is cancelled, already converted, or missing required data.

get.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns a paginated list of branches for the account.

This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token. **Requires the Branches plugin to be enabled on the account.**

The trailing path segment (`1`) is the **data level** — how deeply related records are loaded — not a page number. `/branch/list` and `/branch/list/1` return the same result. Pagination is controlled by the `page` and `per_page` query parameters.

| Parameter | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `page` | Page number (default `1`). |
| `per_page` | Items per page (default `20`). |
| `filter[<field>][<operator>]` | Filter rows by a field's value, e.g. `filter[status][equal]=1`. |
| `sort[<field>]` | Sort by a field, `asc` or `desc`, e.g. `sort[code]=asc`. |

**Filterable fields.** Filter with `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>`. The fields intended for filtering:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `code` | string | `filter[code][equal]=00001` |
| `status` | integer (`1`, `2`, `3`) | `filter[status][equal]=1` |

**Sorting.** Sort with `sort[<field>]=asc|desc`, e.g. `sort[code]=asc`. No field is specifically flagged for sorting; the list will in fact filter and sort on any existing column. When no `sort` is given the default ordering is newest first (`id` descending).

This API exposes six branch fields only — `id`, `name`, `status`, `created`, `modified`, and `code`. Other branch attributes (phone numbers, address, city, state, country, assigned staff, SMTP account, map location) are **not** available through this endpoint.

The `status` value is one of:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `1` | Active |
| `2` | Inactive |
| `3` | Suspended |

This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token. **Requires the Branches plugin to be enabled on the account.**

**This is a partial merge, not a full overwrite.** Only the fields you include in the body are changed; any field you omit is left untouched. The updatable fields are `name`, `code`, and `status`. Only these fields can be updated — `id`, `name`, `status`, `created`, `modified`, and `code`. post.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Create an income.

The request body wraps the income fields in an `Income` object. Optionally include a `JournalTransaction` array to split the amount across chart-of-accounts accounts, a `CostCenterTransaction` array for cost-center allocation, and a `RecurringExpense` object to set up recurrence.

Only `amount` and `date` are required. Most other fields are optional and are defaulted automatically when omitted (see each field). Server-managed fields such as the record type, the recording staff member, and the status are set automatically and cannot be assigned from the request.

**Idempotency:** pass a unique `unique_id` to safely retry. If a previous request with the same `unique_id` already created an income, the response echoes that income (`result` = `duplicated`) instead of creating a duplicate.

**Access:** requires the account owner, or staff holding the *Add New Incomes* (or *Draft*) permission.

amount.description: **Required.** Income amount. Must be non-zero. Treated as gross of any taxes supplied.

date.description: **Required.** Income date, in the account's date format (e.g. `YYYY-MM-DD`). Must fall within an open financial period.

currency_code.description: 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code. Defaults to the account currency when omitted.

category.description: Category name. Created automatically if it does not exist. Alternatively pass `expense_category_id`.

client_id.description: Linked client reference.

supplier_id.description: Linked supplier reference. A suspended supplier is rejected.

treasury_id.description: Treasury to deposit into. Defaults to the primary treasury when omitted.

journal_account_id.description: Journal (chart-of-accounts) account. Optional unless the account is configured to make account selection mandatory and no account is supplied via `JournalTransaction`.

work_order_id.description: Linked work-order reference.

unit_id.description: Rental-unit reference; sets the income source to that unit.

expense_number.description: Income number / reference code. Generated automatically when omitted.

attachment.description: Comma-separated list of previously uploaded file ids to attach. Must be a string; an array is rejected with 400.

unique_id.description: Client-supplied idempotency key. Reusing a key returns the original income instead of creating a duplicate.

tax1_id.description: First tax reference. When omitted, all first-tax fields are cleared.

tax1_value.description: First tax rate (percentage). The tax amount is computed automatically.

tax1_included.description:
Whether the first tax is included in `amount`.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Added on top |
| 1 | Included |

tax2_value.description: Second tax rate (percentage). The tax amount is computed automatically.

tax2_included.description:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Added on top |
| 1 | Included |

JournalTransaction.description: Optional. Splits the income across chart-of-accounts accounts. Entries with an empty `amount` are ignored, and the sum of the remaining amounts must equal `Income.amount`.

amount.description: Portion of the income allocated to this account.

included.description: Whether the line tax is included in the line amount (0/1).

result.description: `successful` for a new income, `duplicated` when an idempotent retry matched an existing one.

id.description: Reference of the created (or existing) income.

MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Create an expense.

The request body wraps the expense fields in an `Expense` object. Optionally include a `JournalTransaction` array to split the amount across chart-of-accounts accounts, a `CostCenterTransaction` array for cost-center allocation, and a `RecurringExpense` object to set up recurrence.

Only `amount` and `date` are required. Most other fields are optional and are defaulted automatically when omitted (see each field). Server-managed fields such as the record type, the recording staff member, and the status are set automatically and cannot be assigned from the request.

**Idempotency:** pass a unique `unique_id` to safely retry. If a previous request with the same `unique_id` already created an expense, the response echoes that expense (`result` = `duplicated`) instead of creating a duplicate.

**Access:** requires the account owner, or staff holding the *Add New Expenses* (or *Draft*) permission.

post.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Creates a follow-up status.

This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token. Send a flat JSON object whose keys are the fields below; `name`, `status`, and `staff_id` are required and any unknown key is ignored.

On success the id of the new status is returned.

item_type.description:
The module/record type this status applies to. Optional — the API does not restrict this field: any integer is accepted, and it defaults to `0` when omitted.

Known values (informational):

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | Client Type |
| 2 | Invoice Type |
| 3 | Estimate Type |
| 4 | PO Type |
| 5 | Staff Type |
| 6 | Supplier Type |
| 7 | Product Type |

The trailing path segment (`1`) is the **data level** — how deeply related records are loaded — not a page number. Pagination is controlled by the `page` and `per_page` query parameters.

Results can be scoped to an approval tab with the `status` query parameter; when it is omitted the request is redirected so that `status=all` is applied by default.

| Parameter | Purpose |

| `page` | Page number (default `1`). |
| `per_page` | Items per page (default `20`). |

| `sort[<field>]` | Sort by a field, `asc` or `desc`. |
| `fields[]` | Restrict the returned columns. |
| `search` | Free-text search. |

**Filterable fields.** Filter with `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>`. The fields intended for filtering:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | `filter[id][equal]=5` |
| `staff_id` | integer (staff) | `filter[staff_id][equal]=1` |
| `type` | enum (`leave`, `half_leave`, `delay`, `early`) | `filter[type][equal]=leave` |
| `date_from` | date | `filter[date_from][greater_than_equal]=2026-01-01` |
| `date_to` | date | `filter[date_to][less_than_equal]=2026-12-31` |

|---|---|---|
| `created` | datetime | `sort[created]=desc` |

This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token. The request body is a **flat JSON object** whose keys are the leave-application fields.

Always provide `staff_id`, `date_from`, `date_to` and `days`. The date range and day count must be consistent: `date_to` must equal `date_from + (days − 1)` (and be on or after `date_from`).

| `delay` | Late Arrival | `late_time` (minutes) |
| `early` | Early Leave | `early_time` (minutes) |

Do **not** send `id` (assigned automatically), `status` (always starts as `pending`), `approved_by`, `created_by` (taken from the authenticated user) or the approval-cycle fields (resolved automatically). post.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Adds a single **component (raw-material) line** to an existing bundle product by creating one product-bundle record.

- `product_id` — the component product to add to the bundle.
- `bundle_product_id` — the existing bundle product the component is attached to.
- `quantity` — how many units of the component the bundle consumes.

Both `product_id` and `bundle_product_id` are required and must reference existing products.

> To build a whole bundle product **and** its lines in one request, create the product entity instead and send the lines as a nested `product_bundles` array; this endpoint adds one line at a time.

product_id.description: Required. The component (raw-material) product to add to the bundle.

bundle_product_id.description: Required. The existing bundle product the component is attached to.

quantity.description: Quantity of the component consumed per bundle unit. Strongly recommended; defaults to `0` when omitted.

unit_name.description: Optional. Display name of the selected unit.

unit_factor.description: Optional. Conversion factor of the selected unit relative to the base unit.

unit_small_name.description: Optional. Display name of the base (small) unit.

unit_factor_id.description: Optional. Identifier of the selected unit factor.

200.description: The component was added to the bundle.

id.description: The id of the newly created product-bundle record.

400.description: The record could not be saved — typically a required field (product_id or bundle_product_id) is missing or invalid.

e.description: Diagnostic details about the failure. May be an empty array when no structured detail is available.

error.description: Human-readable description of why the save failed.

The list can be filtered with the query parameters below. Some filters are only available when the corresponding feature is enabled for the account (noted per parameter).

post.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Creates a new product, service or bundle.

The request body wraps the product fields in a `Product` object. Only `name` is required — every other field is optional and sensible defaults are applied automatically when omitted (for example `type` defaults to Product, `status` to Active, and the taxes to the account's default product taxes).

For bundles (`type = 3`), supply the components in a `ProductBundle` array. Requires a permission that grants the right to add products. On success the new product ID is returned with HTTP 202.

Product type. Defaults to `1` (Product) when omitted.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | Product |
| 2 | Service |
| 3 | Bundle |

|---|---|

tax1.description: First tax ID. Defaults to the account's default product tax when omitted.

tax2.description: Second tax ID. Defaults to the account's second default product tax when omitted.

brand.description: Brand name. Created automatically if it does not yet exist.

category.description: Single category name. Prefer `categories_id` for the API.

tags.description: Tags as a comma-separated string (or an array of strings).

Product status. Defaults to `0` (Active).

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Active |
| 1 | Inactive |
| 2 | Suspended |

tracking_type.description: Stock tracking type. Required when `track_stock` is `1` and the Product Tracking feature is enabled; otherwise defaulted.

initial_stock_level.description: Opening stock quantity. Applied when `track_stock` is `1` and a `store_id` is provided.

store_id.description: Warehouse for the opening stock. Must be an active store.

low_stock_thershold.description: Threshold at which a low-stock notification is raised.

quantity.description: Quantity of that product in the bundle.

put.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Updates an existing product, service or bundle.

This is a partial update — send only the `Product` fields you want to change inside the `Product` object; omitted fields are left unchanged. No field is required.

For bundles, send the full set of components in `ProductBundle` to replace them; omit it to keep the existing components. Some changes are blocked once the product has stock movements — for example you cannot change the bundle type or the stock tracking type when related stock transactions exist. Products are scoped to the current branch. On success the response is a simple confirmation with HTTP 200.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product to update.

type.description:
Product type.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | Product |
| 2 | Service |
| 3 | Bundle |

Discount type.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | Percentage |
| 2 | Absolute |

category.description: Single category name. Prefer `categories_id` for the API.

tags.description: Tags as a comma-separated string (or an array of strings).

Product status.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Active |
| 1 | Inactive |
| 2 | Suspended |

tracking_type.description: Stock tracking type. Cannot be changed once the product has related stock transactions (unless negative tracking is allowed).

initial_stock_level.description: Opening stock quantity. Applied when `track_stock` is `1` and a `store_id` is provided.

store_id.description: Warehouse for the opening stock. Must be an active store.

low_stock_thershold.description: Threshold at which a low-stock notification is raised.

delete.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Deletes a product, service or bundle by its ID.

A product can only be deleted when it has no stock movements and is not tied to a package: if the product has existing stock transactions it cannot be deleted — deactivate it instead. Deleting a product also removes its bundle links and any price-list entries. Products are scoped to the current branch.

On success the response is a confirmation with HTTP 200.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product to delete.

message.description: Confirmation message. Reads "Service has been deleted" when the deleted item is a service.

400.description: The product cannot be deleted: no product ID was supplied, the product is tied to a package, or it fails the deletion eligibility checks.

403.description: The authenticated user lacks permission to delete this product.

404.description: No product matches the given ID, or the product belongs to another branch and is not shared with the current branch.

500.description: The product has existing stock transactions and cannot be deleted (deactivate it instead), or the deletion otherwise failed.

get.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns a paginated list of requisitions (stock transactions: inbound, outbound and transfer movements) as JSON.

Each element of `data` is an object keyed by `Requisition`; the requisition's line items are nested inside it as `RequisitionItem`. Other related records are not included.

When `store_id` is omitted, the list is automatically scoped to the warehouses the authenticated user is allowed to view.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number for pagination. Defaults to `1`.

parameters.name: store_id
parameters.description: Filter to requisitions whose source **or** destination warehouse is this store. When omitted, results are scoped to the warehouses the authenticated user may view.

parameters.name: pos_shift_id
parameters.description: Return only requisitions linked to the given POS shift.

parameters.name: is_stock_request
parameters.description: Set to `1` together with `requisitions_ids` to restrict the result to a specific set of requisitions.

parameters.name: requisitions_ids

parameters.name: is_manufacture_order
parameters.description: Set to `1` together with `manufacturing_order_type` to filter manufacturing-order requisitions.

parameters.name: manufacturing_order_type
parameters.description:
Filter manufacturing-order requisitions by direction. Used together with `is_manufacture_order`.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| inbound | Manufactured product / scrap inbound |
| outbound | Materials issued to the order |
| refund | Returned (refunded) materials |

parameters.name: summary
parameters.description: Set to `1` to request summary mode.

data.description: List of requisitions. Each entry wraps a single requisition under the `Requisition` key, with its line items nested as `RequisitionItem`.

order_type.description: Origin of the requisition (e.g. `1` Inbound, `2` Outbound, `8` Manual Transfer, `25` Sales Order). See the create endpoint for the full list.

post.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Creates a requisition (a stock movement: inbound, outbound or transfer) together with its line items.

The body uses the nested-model convention: a `Requisition` object plus a `RequisitionItem` array. At least one line item is required for a meaningful requisition.

**Required:** `Requisition.store_id` (a valid, active warehouse). Each line item needs a `product_id` and a positive `quantity`.

**Success response** is `{ "status": true, "id": <new id> }` returned with HTTP `200`. Add the `extended` flag to also receive the saved record under `data`.

**Validation failures** return `{ "status": false, "message": ..., "errors": { ... } }` (also HTTP `200`). A line `quantity` of zero or less, or an `attachment` sent as an array instead of a comma-separated string, are rejected with HTTP `400`.

parameters.description: When present, the success response also includes the saved record under `data`.

| 16 | Manufacturing Order Returned Materials |

put.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Updates an existing requisition (identified by its id) and its line items.

The body uses the nested-model convention: a `Requisition` object plus a `RequisitionItem` array, exactly like the create endpoint. On update no header field is strictly required — omitted fields such as `store_id`, `branch_id` and `number` keep / default from the existing record. Each line item still needs a `product_id` and a positive `quantity`.

Some fields are server-managed: a requisition whose status is *Under Delivery* is promoted to *Accepted* on edit, and `number` is generated automatically when left empty.

**Success response** is `{ "status": true, "id": <id> }` at HTTP `200` (add `extended` to also receive the saved record under `data`). A failure to save returns `{ "status": false, "message": "Couldn't update Requisition" }`, also at HTTP 200.

Editing is rejected with `403` for POS / stocktaking requisitions, for a requisition that has expense distribution attached, or for a requisition belonging to another branch.

currency_code.description: Currency code.

number.description: Requisition number. Generated automatically when left empty.

delete.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Deletes a requisition (and its related stock movements) identified by its id.

This is a UI-oriented action and does **not** return a JSON body. To actually delete through the API you must pass `force=1` as a query parameter — without it the request returns the HTML delete-confirmation page and nothing is deleted.

On success the request is redirected (HTTP `302`) to the requisitions list. Pre-delete guards (closed accounting period, another branch, a pending order, a locked item, insufficient stock, tracking, or a linked manufacturing order) also surface as redirects with a flash message rather than a structured JSON error.

To delete a requisition and receive a machine-readable result, prefer the v2 entity API for the `requisition` entity.

put.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Update an existing **Unit Template** (v2 native-entity API).

`PUT https://{subdomain}.daftra.com/v2/api/entity/unit_template/{id}`

## URL rules

- **The record id goes in the path.** `/v2/api/entity/unit_template` without an id is the
  *collection* path — it only accepts `POST` (create). A `PUT` there returns
  `405 The PUT method is not supported for route api/entity/unit_template. Supported methods: POST.`
- **No trailing slash.** A URL ending in `/` is answered with a `301` to the same URL without it,
  and HTTP clients drop the request method **and body** when they follow a `301` — the call arrives
  as a `GET` and you get a misleading "The GET method is not supported" error. Never combine
  `curl --location` with `--request PUT`.

## Authentication

`Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` from the OAuth password grant. The `apikey` header belongs to
the v1 CakePHP `/api2` API and is ignored on this surface.

## Body semantics

- **`id` in the body is what makes this an update.** Omit it and the request **inserts a new record**
  and returns the new id — the `{id}` in the URL does not prevent that. Always send `id`, matching the URL.
- Fields you omit keep their stored value (partial merge)…
- …**except `active`, which is a checkbox: omitting it stores `0`.** Send it on every update.
- `branch_id` and `staff_id` are assigned by the server (auto-branch / auto-staff) and ignored if sent.
- `created` / `modified` are read-only.

## Unit factors

- The array key is **`unit_templates_unit_factors`** (parent table + subform name). `unit_factors`
  is silently ignored — the rows are dropped without an error.
- The array **replaces the whole set**: a row **with** `id` is updated, a row **without** `id` is
  inserted, and any existing row you leave out is **deleted**.
- Omit the key entirely to leave the existing factors untouched.

## Responses

| Code | Body | When |
| ---- | ---- | ---- |
| 200 | `{message, id}` | Saved. `message` is localised to the site language — match on the status and `id`, not the text. |
| 400 | `{message}` or `{message, errors}` | `Record not found` for an unknown id, or `Entity not saved` with per-field errors. |
| 401 | `{error}` | Caller lacks the update permission for this entity. |
| 405 | `{message}` | Wrong method for the path — usually a missing id or a followed trailing-slash redirect (see *URL rules*). |

Server-controlled fields are set automatically and ignored if supplied: the source is fixed to *Manual*, the status to *Processed*, and `order_id`, `staff_id`, and `branch_id` are assigned by the server.

On success the endpoint responds with **202 Accepted** and the new transaction id.

Requires the **Adjust Product Inventory** permission.

This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token.

The trailing path segment (`1`) is the **data level** — how deeply related records are loaded — not a page number. `/credit_charge/list` and `/credit_charge/list/1` return the same result. Pagination is controlled by the `page` and `per_page` query parameters.

| Parameter | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `page` | Page number (default `1`). |
| `per_page` | Items per page (default `20`). |
| `filter[<field>][<operator>]` | Filter rows by a field's value, e.g. `filter[client_id][equal]=8` or `filter[status][equal]=available`. |
| `sort[<field>]` | Sort by a field, `asc` or `desc`, e.g. `sort[amount]=desc`. |

**Filterable fields.** The fields intended for filtering:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `staff_id` | integer (staff) | `filter[staff_id][equal]=1` |
| `client_id` | integer (client) | `filter[client_id][equal]=8` |
| `credit_type_id` | integer (credit type) | `filter[credit_type_id][equal]=1` |
| `status` | enum (`available`, `consumed`, `expired`, `suspended`) | `filter[status][equal]=available` |
| `start_date` | date | `filter[start_date][greater_than_equal]=2025-01-01` |
| `expiry_date` | date | `filter[expiry_date][less_than_equal]=2026-12-31` |
| `amount` | number | `filter[amount][greater_than]=10` |

The list will in fact filter and sort on any existing column, not only the fields above. When no `sort` is given the default ordering is newest first (`id` descending).

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `available` | Credit is available to consume |
| `consumed` | Credit has been fully used |
| `expired` | Credit passed its expiry date |
| `suspended` | Credit is temporarily suspended |

This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token. The trailing path segment (`1`) is the **data level** — how deeply related records are loaded — not a page number; on this endpoint it has no visible effect. The response is a flat credit-usage record.

post.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Updates an existing credit usage. This posts to the same `/v2/api/entity/credit_usage` path as create; the record to update is identified by the **`id` in the request body**. If `id` is omitted a new record is created instead.

**Important — this is a partial overwrite, not a full merge.** The update always rewrites the foreign-key columns `client_id` and `credit_type_id` and sets either of them **that you omit to null**. Because both are non-nullable, omitting one fails with a `400`. **Always resend `client_id` and `credit_type_id` on every update.** The other fields (`usage_date`, `description`) are preserved if omitted.

`usage_date` accepts `YYYY-MM-DD` or `DD/MM/YYYY`. On success the response is `{ "message": <localized text>, "id": <id> }`.

id.description: Id of the credit usage to update. Required — omitting it creates a new record instead.

client_id.description: Id of the client. Part of the core overwrite set — resend it or it is set to null (→ 400, non-nullable).

credit_type_id.description: Id of the credit type. Part of the core overwrite set — resend it or it is set to null (→ 400, non-nullable).

usage_date.description: Date the credit was used. Optional; preserved if omitted. Accepts `YYYY-MM-DD` or `DD/MM/YYYY`.

description.description: Free-text note. Optional; preserved if omitted.

id.description: Id of the updated credit usage.

400.description: The update could not be saved — most commonly because a core foreign key (`client_id` or `credit_type_id`) was omitted and nulled a non-nullable column.

error.description: Human-readable failure reason (e.g. a core-set foreign key was omitted and nulled a non-nullable column).

get.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns a paginated list of charge usage records. A charge usage links a credit charge to a credit usage and stores the amount consumed.

This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token.

The trailing path segment (`1`) is the **data level** — how deeply related records are loaded — not a page number. `/charge_usage/list` and `/charge_usage/list/1` return the same result. Pagination is controlled by the `page` and `per_page` query parameters.

| Parameter | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `page` | Page number (default `1`). |
| `per_page` | Items per page (default `20`). |
| `filter[<field>][<operator>]` | Filter rows by a field's value, e.g. `filter[credit_usage_id][equal]=5`. |
| `sort[<field>]` | Sort by a field, `asc` or `desc`, e.g. `sort[amount]=desc`. |

**Filterable fields.** The fields intended for filtering:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `credit_charge_id` | integer (credit charge) | `filter[credit_charge_id][equal]=12` |
| `credit_usage_id` | integer (credit usage) | `filter[credit_usage_id][equal]=5` |
| `amount` | number | `filter[amount][greater_than]=10` |

The list will in fact filter and sort on any existing column, not only the fields above. When no `sort` is given the default ordering is newest first (`id` descending).

Each item in `data` is a flat charge-usage record.

get.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns a **paginated** list of credit types.

A credit type defines a kind of credit/points balance (e.g. loyalty points). The response is a standard paginated envelope: the records are in `data[]` (each item is `id`, `name`, `allow_decimal`, `status`, `unit`, `description`, `created`, `modified`, `deleted_at`), alongside pagination metadata (`current_page`, `per_page`, `total`, `last_page`, `from`, `to`, `links`, and the `*_page_url` fields).

| Parameter | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `page` | Page number (default `1`). |
| `per_page` | Items per page (default `20`). |
| `filter[<field>][<operator>]` | Filter by a field (see Filterable fields below). |
| `sort[<field>]` | Sort by a field, `asc` or `desc`. |
| `fields[]` | Restrict the returned columns. |

**Filterable fields.** Filter with `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>`:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | `filter[name][like]=Loyalty` |
| `status` | enum (`0` Inactive, `1` Active) | `filter[status][equal]=1` |

In practice the endpoint filters and sorts on any existing column. With no `sort`, results default to newest-first (by `id`).

The trailing path segment sets the data-detail level (e.g. `/credit_type/list/1`); it is optional for this entity and does not change the returned records — it is only echoed back into the pagination URLs.

get.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns a paginated list of packages (membership and credit-charge packages) for the account.

### Ordering
Newest first — `id` descending — unless you pass a `sort` parameter.

### Branch scoping
When the Branches add-on is enabled, results are automatically limited to your current branch. To widen the scope:

| Goal | How |
|---|---|
| A specific branch | `request_branch_id=<branch id>` |
| Every branch you have access to | `filter[branch_id][equal]=-1` |

Packages stored without a branch are not returned while branch scoping is in effect.

### Deleted packages
Deleted packages are excluded, so `deleted_at` is always `null` in this response. Fetch a deleted package directly by its id if you need it.

### Filtering
Use `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>`. Omitting the operator means `equal` — `filter[status]=1` is the same as `filter[status][equal]=1`.

| Operator | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `equal` | equals (default) |
| `not_equal` | not equal |
| `in` / `not_in` | in / not in a list of values |
| `like` | partial text match |
| `gt` / `gte` / `from` | greater than / greater than or equal |
| `lt` / `lte` / `to` | less than / less than or equal |
| `is_null` / `is_not_null` | value is / is not empty |

Fields intended for filtering: `name`, `price`, `period_value`, `status`, `product_id`. Filtering on an unrecognised field returns `400`.

### Sorting
Use `sort[<field>]=asc` or `sort[<field>]=desc`, e.g. `sort[name]=asc`.

### Notes
- The trailing `1` in the path is an optional data-detail level. It has no effect for packages, which are always returned as flat records.
- A `fields[]` parameter is not supported; the complete record is always returned.

post.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Updates an existing package. The package is identified by the **`id` in the request body** — this endpoint uses the same URL as *Add New Package*.

### `id` selects the record
A body **without** `id` creates a new package instead of updating one, and still replies with an "Added Successfully" message. Always send `id`.

### Only the fields you send are changed — with two exceptions
Fields you leave out keep their current values. The exceptions are the two reference fields:

| Field | Left out of the body |
|---|---|
| `branch_id` | **Set to `null`** — the package loses its branch and stops appearing in *Get All Packages* |
| `product_id` | **Set to `null`** — the package is unlinked from its product |

So resend `branch_id` and `product_id` on every update, even when they are not changing.

### Clearing a text value
Sending `null` for `name`, `description`, `price`, `period_value`, `period_unit`, `status` or `type` leaves the current value untouched. Send an empty string (`""`) to clear a text field.

### Send `Accept: application/json`
This endpoint answers with a redirect to a web page instead of JSON when the request does not ask for JSON. Always send `Accept: application/json`.

### Other notes
- A successful update replies `Package Added Successfully` — the same wording as a create. Do not read it as proof that a new package was inserted; check the `id` you sent.
- An `id` that does not exist returns `400` with `"error": "Record Not Found"`, not `404`.
- Body keys that are not package fields are ignored silently — a misspelled field name is not reported as an error.
- `modified` is refreshed automatically; `created` and `deleted_at` should be omitted.
- Values are not validated against the lists below before they reach the database, so an out-of-range value fails as a save error rather than a field-level validation error.

id.description: Id of the package to update. **Required** — without it a new package is created.

name.description: Package name. Optional — unchanged when omitted.

period_value.description: How many `period_unit` intervals the package covers. Optional — unchanged when omitted.

period_unit.description:
The unit the validity period is counted in. Optional — unchanged when omitted.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `daily` | Days |
| `weekly` | Weeks |
| `monthly` | Months |
| `yearly` | Years |
| `not-expired` | Never expires |

price.description: Package price; decimals are allowed. Optional — unchanged when omitted.

type.description:
What the package sells. Optional — unchanged when omitted.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `credit_charge` | A bundle of credits |
| `membership` | A membership subscription |

status.description:
Whether the package can be sold. Optional — unchanged when omitted.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Inactive |
| 1 | Active |

description.description: Free-text description. Optional — unchanged when omitted. Send `""` to clear it.

product_id.description: Id of the product the package is linked to. **Resend on every update** — when omitted it is set to `null`.

branch_id.description: Branch the package belongs to. **Resend on every update** — when omitted it is set to `null` and the package stops appearing in *Get All Packages*.

message.description: Confirmation message. Uses the create wording even for an update.

id.description: Id of the package that was updated — the value you sent.

400.description: The package was not updated.

message.description: `Entity not saved` when the update could not be applied — the `id` does not exist, or a value fell outside an allowed list. `Plugin is not installed` when the Points & Credits add-on is not active for the account.

error.description: Reason for the failure — `Record Not Found` for an unknown `id`, otherwise the database-level reason. Present only on the save-failure variant.

e.description: Diagnostic detail about the failure. Present only on the save-failure variant; treat as opaque and do not depend on its shape.

error.description: Returned instead of `message` when the account is authenticated but not permitted to save packages.

get.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns a paginated list of purchase debit notes for the account. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token. It requires the **Inventory** plugin to be active.

A purchase debit note is a purchase document that shares storage with purchase orders and is identified by its document type. This endpoint returns only debit-note records.

### Data-level path segment

The trailing path segment (`-1`) is the **relation data level** — how deeply related records are eager-loaded — not a page number. Use `-1` (load base record with light relations only). Calling the list **without** a data level (`.../purchase_debit_note/list`) attempts to eager-load the full relation graph and fails with a `400` database error, so always include the segment.

### Pagination & query parameters

| Parameter | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `page` | Page number (default `1`). |
| `per_page` | Items per page (default `20`). |
| `filter[<field>]` | Filter by a field's value, e.g. `filter[no]=PDN-0001` or `filter[supplier_id]=1`. |
| `sort[<field>]` | Sort by a field, `asc` or `desc`, e.g. `sort[date]=desc`. Default ordering is newest first (`id` descending). |
| `version` | Set to `2` to run each row through the listing formatter (adds display-formatted values); the top-level envelope is unchanged. |

**Filterable fields.** Filter with `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>` (the operator is optional; `filter[<field>]=<value>` uses a default match). The fields intended for filtering:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `no` | string | `filter[no]=PDN-0001` |
| `supplier_id` | integer (supplier) | `filter[supplier_id]=1` |
| `date` | date | `filter[date][greater_than_equal]=2026-01-01` |
| `summary_total` | number | `filter[summary_total][greater_than_equal]=100` |
| `tags` | string | `filter[tags]=urgent` |

**Sortable fields.** Sort with `sort[<field>]=asc|desc`. The fields intended for sorting:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `date` | date | `sort[date]=desc` |
| `no` | string | `sort[no]=asc` |
| `created` | datetime | `sort[created]=desc` |

The API will in fact filter and sort on any existing column of the record; the tables above list the fields the product surfaces for this entity. With no `sort`, results are ordered by `id` descending.

### Response

The response is a standard paginated envelope (`current_page`, `data`, `per_page`, `total`, `last_page`, and the page-URL/link fields). Each item in `data` is a flat purchase debit note record.

`payment_status` and `requisition_delivery_status` are returned as codes; their meanings are listed on those fields below.

parameters.description: Relation eager-loading depth. Use `-1` (base record with light relations only). Omitting the segment entirely (`.../list`) attempts to load the full relation graph and fails with a `400` database error, so a value is required.

parameters.description: Page number. Defaults to `1`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Items per page. Defaults to `20`.

post.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Creates a purchase debit note. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token. It requires the **Inventory** plugin to be active.

A purchase debit note shares storage with purchase orders and is identified by its document type, so **`type` must be `14`** — sending a different type (or omitting it) fails with a `400` (`"error": "Record Not Found"`) because the entity can only be resolved for type `14`.

### Request body

The body is a flat JSON object. The account layer enforces exactly three required fields — omitting any of them returns `422`:

| Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| `supplier_business_name` | Required, non-empty. |
| `draft` | Required. `1` = save as draft, `0` = finalized. |
| `summary_total.currency` | Required, non-empty (the currency of the totals object). |

In addition, `type` must be `14` for the record to save (enforced below the validation layer with a `400`).

All other fields are optional. `no` (the debit-note number) is generated automatically when omitted. `currency_code` and `supplier_id` are optional. Server-managed fields (`id`, `created`, `modified`, `branch_id`, `site_id`, `staff_id`, payment/summary totals) are assigned by the server.

### Line items

Line items are sent under the **`purchase_debit_notes_items`** array (each entry becomes a purchase-order-item row). Each item takes `product_id`, `item` (name), `description`, `unit_price`, `quantity`, `discount`, `discount_type`, `tax1`, `tax2`, and optional `col_3`..`col_5` extra columns.

### Statuses

`requisition_delivery_status`:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | Received |
| 2 | Rejected |
| 3 | Pending |
| 4 | Partially Received |
| 5 | Partially Rejected |

On success the response is `{ "message": "...", "id": <new id> }`; the message is localized to the caller's language.

MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Assigns a work order to an existing invoice (or clears the assignment).

Send the target work order ID nested under the `Invoice` object as `work_order_id`. The invoice is identified by the `id` path parameter. To remove an existing assignment, send `work_order_id` as `0` or empty.

The `Invoice` object is required: if it is omitted the request is rejected with `403` and the message `Please send valid work order id`.

Requires permission to edit the invoice. If the Accounting module is enabled, the invoice's date must not fall within a closed financial period, otherwise the request is rejected with `400`.

Work orders are part of the Work Orders feature; assigning an ID is only meaningful when that feature is enabled for your account.

post.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Sets shipping details on an existing invoice.

The invoice is identified by the `id` path parameter. Send the shipping fields nested under the `Invoice` object — all are optional, and only the fields you include (with a non-empty value) are applied:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `shipping_option_id` | ID of a shipping option to apply |
| `shipping_amount` | Shipping fee added to the invoice total |
| `shipping_tax_id` | ID of the tax applied to the shipping fee |
| `shipping_number` | Tracking/shipping number, recorded as the invoice's "Shipping Number" custom field |

Empty or `0` values are ignored, so this endpoint can set or overwrite shipping fields but cannot clear them. A request that includes no shipping fields still returns a success response without changing the invoice.

The response is `403` when no invoice matches the given ID.

post.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Converts a sales order (identified by the `id` path parameter) into a new invoice.

The new invoice inherits the sales order's client, currency, shipping, discounts, adjustment, and a source link back to the sales order — these are taken from the sales order and **override** any values you send. Send `InvoiceItem` to choose which lines and quantities to convert (**partial conversion** is supported); you may also pass standard invoice fields such as `date`, `store_id`, or `draft`.

If the sales order has requisitions, conversion is limited to accepted/selected requisition lines — pass `requisition_ids[]` (query) to choose them when you hold the convert permission.

On success the invoice is created and returned with the standard creation envelope (HTTP `202` with the new invoice `id`). Requires the Sales Order module to be enabled and permission to create invoices / convert sales orders. The request is rejected with `404` when the sales order is missing, already invoiced, not permitted, or has no convertible items.

parameters.description: The sales order ID to convert.

parameters.name: requisition_ids[]
parameters.description: When the sales order has requisitions, the ids of the requisitions to convert. Repeat the key for multiple ids. Only applies with the convert-sales-order permission.

InvoiceItem.description: The sales-order lines (and quantities) to convert. Supports partial conversion — send only the items/quantities you want invoiced. Same line shape as Add New Invoice.

Invoice.description: Optional invoice fields passed through to creation (for example `date`, `store_id`, `draft`). Note: client, currency, shipping, discounts, and the source link are copied from the sales order and override any value sent here.

store_id.description: Store / warehouse for stock deduction. Defaults to the primary store.

draft.description: Create the invoice as a draft.

404.description: Returned for several conditions: the sales order does not exist, the Sales Order module is disabled, the caller lacks permission to invoice this client, the sales order is already invoiced (or no convertible items were supplied), or its requisitions are not in a convertible state.

Requires the Sales Order module to be enabled and permission to delete sales orders (a non-owner may delete only their own unless they hold the delete-all permission).

A sales order **cannot** be deleted once it has been invoiced or partially invoiced, or while it is linked to a production plan — such requests are rejected with `400`. On success the response is `200` with a confirmation message.

parameters.description: The sales order ID to delete.

Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns a paginated list of the account's **subscriptions** (recurring invoices), most recent first.

The request body has the same shape as **Add New Invoice** (an `Invoice` object plus optional `InvoiceItem`, `Payment`, etc.); a `RefundReceipt` object is also accepted in place of `Invoice`. Send the fields you want to change; the id from the path is always applied.

Returns `404` when no refund receipt matches the id; editing is also blocked (`404`) when the refund receipt has been submitted to a tax authority. Requires permission to edit invoices/refund receipts. See **Add New Invoice** for the full field reference.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The refund receipt ID to update.

Invoice.description: Refund-receipt header fields to update. Same fields as the Add New Invoice header (a `RefundReceipt` key is also accepted in place of `Invoice`).

date.description: Refund-receipt date (YYYY-MM-DD).

currency_code.description: Currency code (for example, USD).

store_id.description: Store / warehouse for line items.

InvoiceItem.description: Refund-receipt line items. Same shape as Add New Invoice line items.

400.description: Validation failed, or a selected store/product is inactive or violates its minimum price / stock.

validation_errors.description: Field-level error messages, present when validation fails.

403.description: The authenticated user lacks permission to edit this refund receipt.

404.description: No refund receipt matches the id, or it cannot be edited (e.g. submitted to a tax authority).

delete.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Deletes a refund receipt identified by the `id` path parameter.

Requires permission to delete invoices/refund receipts (a non-owner may delete only refund receipts they created unless they hold the delete-all permission). One refund receipt is deleted per call.

A refund receipt **cannot be deleted** while it is blocked by a business rule — for example it belongs to a closed POS session, has an approved requisition, has linked documents, or has been submitted to a tax authority; these are rejected with HTTP `401` (see the response below). On success the response is `200` with a confirmation message.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The refund receipt ID to delete.

400.description: No refund receipt id was supplied, or a stock-balance check prevents the deletion.

401.description: The refund receipt cannot be deleted because of a business rule (closed POS session, approved requisition, linked documents, submitted to a tax authority, locked item, etc.).

403.description: The authenticated user lacks permission to delete refund receipts.

404.description: No refund receipt matches the given ID (or it is not accessible to the authenticated user).

500.description: The deletion failed unexpectedly.

post.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Creates multiple refund receipts in a single request. The request body is a **JSON array**; each element has the same shape as the body of **Add New Refund Receipt** (an object with an `Invoice` member — `RefundReceipt` is also accepted — plus optional `InvoiceItem`, `Payment`, etc.).

Each element must set `Invoice.subscription_id` to the **source invoice being refunded** (despite the name, this is not a subscription). That source invoice must be an issued (non-draft) standard invoice.

Refund receipts are created **one by one and the operation is not atomic** — if one element fails the others are still created. The response is a **JSON array** with one result object per submitted element, in request order:

| Outcome | Item fields |
|---|---|
| Success | `result` = `successful`, `code` = `202`, `id`, `invoice_number` |
| Failure | `message`, `validation_errors` (and sometimes `error_type` / `extra_data`) |

The overall response is `200` regardless of individual outcomes, so you must inspect each element. Per-element field and defaulting behaviour is identical to **Add New Refund Receipt** — see that endpoint for the full field reference.

schema.description: Array of refund receipts to create. Each element has the same shape as the body of Add New Refund Receipt (an object with an `Invoice` member plus optional `InvoiceItem`, `Payment`, etc.).

Invoice.description: Refund receipt header. The `RefundReceipt` key is also accepted and treated as `Invoice`.

subscription_id.description: **Required.** The ID of the source invoice being refunded (despite the field name, this is not a subscription). The source invoice must be an issued (non-draft) standard invoice. An element with no `subscription_id` fails with `Invoice not found`.

date.description: Refund receipt date (YYYY-MM-DD). Must fall within an open financial period.

currency_code.description: Currency code (for example, `USD`). Optional — defaults to the account currency.

InvoiceItem.description: Line items being refunded. Same shape as Add New Refund Receipt / Add New Invoice line items.

200.description: All elements processed. Each array element is either a success object (`result`/`code`/`id`/`invoice_number`) or an error object (`message`/`validation_errors`).

schema.description: One result object per submitted element, in request order. A 200 does not guarantee every refund receipt was created — inspect each element. Successful items carry the created refund receipt id/number; failed items carry an error result.

code.description: Present on successful items.

id.description: The new refund receipt id (successful items).

invoice_number.description: The generated refund receipt number (successful items).

validation_errors.description: Field-level or general error messages (failed items).

extra_data.description: Additional error context, when set (failed items).

403.description: You do not have permission to create refund receipts. Note: a permission failure (or a draft source invoice) on any single element can abort the whole batch with this status rather than failing only that element.

get.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. List invoice payments, most recent first.

Returns a paginated array under `data[]`, each entry wrapped in an `InvoicePayment` object, plus a `pagination` summary. Only payments linked to an invoice are returned.

By default, `client_credit` and opening-balance (`starting_balance`) payments are **excluded**. Pass `include_starting_balance=1` to include opening-balance payments, or set `payment_method` explicitly to target one of them.

Results can be narrowed with the query filters below and ordered with `sort`/`direction` (default: newest first).

**Access:** available to the account owner, or to staff holding any of the *View Invoice Details*, *View All Invoices*, *Add Invoice Payments*, or *Add Payments to All* permissions.

post.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Record a payment against an invoice.

Send the payment under an `InvoicePayment` object. To create several payments in one call, send an **array** of payment objects under `InvoicePayment` instead.

**Required:** `invoice_id`, `amount`, and `payment_method`. `payment_method` must be one of the account's active configured payment methods (e.g. `cash`, `bank`, `cheque`, or an enabled online gateway key).

Several fields are set automatically and cannot be supplied by the caller: the payment `status` (new payments are marked Completed), the recording staff, the currency (taken from the invoice), and the payer contact details (name/address are copied from the invoice's client). Any such fields included in the request are ignored.

On success the endpoint responds with `202 Accepted` and the new payment `id`.

treasury_id.description: Optional treasury to deposit into. Chosen automatically from the payment method or your default treasury when omitted.

pos_shift_id.description: Optional point-of-sale shift reference, for POS payments.

put.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Update an existing invoice payment.

This is a partial update — send only the fields you want to change, under an `InvoicePayment` object. Fields not listed below (and any read-only fields) are ignored.

**Editable fields** (for payments recorded by staff/API): `amount`, `date`, `payment_method`, `transaction_id`, `treasury_id`, `status`, `notes`, `receipt_notes`, `currency_code`, `staff_id`, `invoice_id`, `extra_details`, `attachment`. If the payment was recorded by a client, only a narrower set is editable: `treasury_id`, `receipt_notes`, `status`, `notes`, `invoice_id`, `attachment`.

Notes: `payment_method`, if changed, must be one of the account's active configured methods (changing it clears stored gateway metadata). Changing the payment `date` requires the relevant permission; otherwise the original date is kept.

MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Delete an invoice payment by its id.

Removing the payment re-adjusts the related invoice's paid total and the client's balance, and removes any attachments linked to the payment.

**Access:** requires permission to edit/remove invoice payments — either across all payments, or limited to the caller's own payments. Payments tied to an advance-payment invoice, and (when automatic invoice payment is enabled) client-credit payments, cannot be deleted via the API.

get.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns the account's **active** shipping options — the named delivery methods (each with a fee and an optional tax) that can be applied to invoices.

Notes:

- Only active shipping options are returned; disabled or removed ones are omitted.
- This endpoint is **not paginated** — every active shipping option is returned in a single `data` array, and `page` / `limit` query parameters are ignored.
- It takes no query parameters and no request body.
- Each item exposes `tax_id` as a plain identifier; the related tax record is not embedded.

Requires a valid bearer token; no additional permission is needed.

display_order.description: Position used when ordering shipping options for display.

status.description:
Whether the shipping option is active. Only active options are returned by this endpoint.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Inactive |
| 1 | Active |

description.description: Optional free-text description of the shipping option.

created.description: Time the shipping option was created.

modified.description: Time the shipping option was last updated.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete timestamp. Always `null` for options returned by this endpoint.

get.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns the configuration for the **currently open POS shift session** — the data a point-of-sale client needs to bootstrap a session: the active language and default payment method, the session's branch and store, the cashier, cash-in/cash-out links, and a set of capability and feature flags derived from your permissions and account settings.

The session is identified by the open shift bound to your authenticated session, or by the `Posshift` request header carrying the POS shift session id when no session binding exists.

Returns **200** only when the shift is open and you are allowed to access it (you opened it and may open your own sessions, or you may open all sessions). Some members of `Shift` appear only when the related feature is enabled — the embedded-barcode lengths when embedded barcodes are configured, and the insurance members when the Insurance feature is active.

get.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns information about the current site (account) and the authenticated principal: the business/owner profile, localization (currency, number and date formats), subscription status, and a few plugin/context flags. The payload is wrapped in a `Site` object under `data`.

Some fields are conditional:
- `is_super_admin` and `staff` are returned only when the request is authenticated as a staff member (`staff_id` > 0); `staff` is that staff member's record with the password removed.
- `expensesIsMandatoryEnabled` is returned only when the request sends the header `x-app-name: EXP`.

Authenticate with an `apikey` header or a Bearer access token.
